decisions.source_issue: R48–51 and P6–16 describe ten plants and detailed recipes, while current identity, role and product status cannot be inferred from a common name.
decisions.decision: Use botanical names and reference-card matching; treat listed use as a consultation topic. Exclude practical identification from a drawing, dosing, ingestion and unsupervised preparation.
decisions.remaining: Qualified botanical/clinical reviewer and local health center must confirm specimens, parts, approved products and authorized training.

decisions.source_issue: Legacy text can be read as permission to replace diabetes, cholesterol or gout treatment with plant food or decoctions.
decisions.decision: Identify listed leaf/bulb/top and the source-associated topic; never stop or modify prescribed treatment. Return management to the supervising clinician.
decisions.remaining: Check current local protocols, interactions, contraindications and product registration.

decisions.source_issue: A local plant name and old topical recipe may be misapplied to a different plant or an infected wound.
decisions.decision: Teach reference identity and part only; do not prescribe topical preparation. Escalate worsening skin disease or signs of wound infection.
decisions.remaining: Qualified review of diagnosis boundaries, skin/wound products, adverse reactions and local referral.

decisions.source_issue: Cough, abdominal pain and toothache may need assessment; legacy recipes and age tables are not a blanket BHW dosing protocol.
decisions.decision: Link the source-associated plant and part to the symptom topic while identifying urgent or persistent concerns for clinical or dental assessment. Omit numeric recipes.
decisions.remaining: Confirm current product labels, contraindications, pediatric boundaries and local clinical guidance.

decisions.source_issue: Seed counts and decoction recipes could delay safe deworming or assessment of urinary pain and low urine output.
decisions.decision: Teach part and source-associated topic, but refer suspected worms and concerning urinary symptoms for diagnosis and treatment. Do not give seeds or promise stone resolution.
decisions.remaining: Qualified review of deworming, urologic referral, plant toxicity and authorized preparations.

directory_count_discrepancy: The PITAHC Directory of Herbs page says “9 herbs” but contains ten named plant sections. The ten source-manual lessons are retained; current official list status requires owner/local confirmation.
